post.description: Create a user, their first organisation, and their owner membership.

Revoke every session for this user.

Real revocation is the reason sessions are server-side. This is what makes
"I think my laptop was stolen" an action rather than a wait.

get.description:
Every organisation this user belongs to.

Scoped by membership rather than by RLS: the caller has no active tenant yet
at this point, which is exactly the state this endpoint exists to resolve.

schema.title: Response List Organizations V1 Organizations Get

post.description:
Change the active organisation on the current session.

Membership is re-checked here rather than trusted from the request: without
this check, switching would be a self-service grant of access to any
organisation whose ID the caller can guess.

schema.title: Response List Members V1 Organizations Members Get

post.description:
Add an existing user to this organisation.

An admin cannot grant a role above their own — otherwise "admin" is
functionally "owner" via one extra call.

schema.title: Response List Apps V1 Apps Get

delete.description:
Disable, never delete.

Deleting an app would cascade to its campaigns and attribution history —
numbers a client may have already reported to an ad network. Disabling stops
ingestion and leaves the record intact.

"Stops ingestion" has to be true now rather than eventually. The tracker
authenticates against a cached key record that carries the app's status, so
without clearing those entries a disabled app kept accepting events for up
to ten minutes — and its links kept redirecting until the link cache was
told, which is what the notification below is for.

get.description:
Keys are admin-visible only.

A viewer can read analytics; a viewer who can enumerate key prefixes and
revoke credentials can take an advertiser's tracking offline.

schema.title: Response List Keys V1 Apps  App Id  Keys Get

post.description:
Issue a replacement key and revoke the old one.

The new key is created before the old one is revoked, inside a transaction,
so the caller never holds zero working credentials at any instant.

That is the only overlap there is. The old key stops working immediately —
the database says revoked and the tracker's cache is cleared to match, the
same as an outright revocation, because rotation is usually done for the
same reason. This used to leave the old key live for up to ten minutes: the
row said revoked and the cache had not been told, so the grace period was an
accident of a TTL rather than anything anyone chose.

A genuine timed overlap — old key valid until a stated moment — would be a
`revoke_at` column and a deliberate feature, not a stale cache.

schema.title: Response List Campaigns V1 Campaigns Get
Response List Links V1 Tracking Links Get

delete.description:
Disable, never delete.

Clicks already recorded reference this link, and an advertiser's historical
reporting must not develop holes because someone tidied up.

get.description:
Attribution counts by method over a bounded range.

The date range is required rather than defaulted. A default would be a
default *scan*, and the first person to open this on a large advertiser
would discover how large by waiting for it.

Every attribution ever recorded for one device, newest first.

Includes superseded rows deliberately. "It used to say organic and now it
says Meta" is a question we must be able to answer with the record rather
than with an explanation, and the superseded chain is that record.

Response Campaigns V1 Analytics Campaigns Get
Response Events V1 Analytics Events Get
Response List Rules V1 Postback Rules Get

delete.description:
Disable, not delete.

Delivery rows reference this rule, and a deleted rule would leave an
advertiser unable to explain conversions their network already received.

get.description:
What a template may reference, so a form can list it from the source of
truth rather than from a copy that drifts.

schema.title: Response Postback Variables V1 Postback Rules Variables Get

get.description:
Render the templates against sample values.

Lets someone see the URL their partner will actually receive before any real
conversion depends on it — which is the difference between finding a
misplaced parameter now and finding it in a reconciliation meeting.

Recent delivery attempts, newest first.

Bounded and never open-ended: this table is the busiest write target in the
system, and an unpaginated listing of it is a query that gets slower every
day until someone notices.

schema.title: Response List Deliveries V1 Postback Deliveries Get

post.description:
Queue one failed delivery for another attempt.

Only from a terminal failed state. Re-queueing something already in flight
would let an impatient click produce the duplicate conversion the whole
delivery design exists to prevent.

schema.title: Response List Webhooks V1 Webhooks Get

post.description:
Issue a new signing secret.

Deliveries are signed with the new secret immediately, so the receiver must
be updated first — there is no dual-signing period. That is a deliberate
simplification: accepting two secrets at once doubles the window in which a
leaked one still works, and rotation is rare enough to coordinate.

delete.description:
Genuinely deleted, unlike a postback rule.

A webhook is the customer's own integration, not a record of what an ad
network was told. Nothing downstream needs to explain it later, and leaving
a disabled row holding an encrypted secret serves nobody.

schema.title: Response Available Events V1 Webhooks Events Get
Response List Deliveries V1 Webhooks  Webhook Id  Deliveries Get

get.description:
Everything a device has told this app, purpose by purpose.

Both parameters required: an unfiltered listing of consent records is a
listing of every device in the app, which is neither useful nor something
this endpoint should make easy.

schema.title: Response List Consent V1 Privacy Consent Get

post.description:
Record a decision made outside the SDK.

A consent management platform, a support agent acting on a written request,
a backfill. The SDK's own path goes through the tracker as an ordinary
event; this is for everything else.

Erase a device's data, and record that we did.

Admin-only: this is destructive and irreversible, and a viewer's job is to
read reports.

Performed synchronously here because the volume for one device is small and
a caller answering a regulator wants a completed result, not a ticket. A
bulk erasure — a whole app, a whole organisation — would need the async path
described in mmp_db.erasure, and does not exist yet.

get.description:
Walk the audit chain and report the first entry that does not match.

A chain nobody verifies is a chain nobody would notice was broken.

The adapters this build has.

Read from the registry rather than a hard-coded list, so a deployment cannot
advertise an integration it cannot actually perform.

schema.title: Response List Providers V1 Providers Get

get.description:
Admin-only: an integration list is a list of which networks an advertiser
works with, which is commercially sensitive even without the credentials.

schema.title: Response List Integrations V1 Integrations Get

delete.description:
Deleting sets any rule using it back to the plain template path.

The foreign key is ON DELETE SET NULL rather than CASCADE, deliberately:
removing an integration should not silently delete the postback rules an
advertiser configured, and a rule with no provider still works.

get.description:
What this integration will accept.

Lets a dashboard refuse to attach a refund rule to a provider that does not
take refunds, rather than letting someone configure a delivery the network
will silently discard.

schema.title: Response Integration Capabilities V1 Integrations  Integration Id  Capabilities Get

Response List Deep Links V1 Deep Links Get

get.description:
Admin-only. An export is the whole dataset leaving the system, which is a
different act from reading a report, and should need a different level of
authority.

schema.title: Response List Conversion Values V1 Skan Conversion Values Get

put.description:
Upsert, not create.

An advertiser tunes this mapping repeatedly while working out what their 64
values should mean, and a create-only endpoint would make every adjustment a
delete followed by a create — with a window in between where the event maps
to nothing at all.

schema.title: Response List Postbacks V1 Skan Postbacks Get

get.description:
Grouped by network and campaign, with the withheld values counted.

``suppressed`` is reported rather than hidden: a campaign whose conversion
values were mostly withheld has an average computed from the few that were
not, and an average over an unstated fraction of the data is exactly the
kind of number that gets quoted without its denominator.

Recent activity for one app, newest first.

Poll with the ``server_time`` from the previous response as ``since``. Each
poll deliberately re-reads the minute before it (see ``LATE_WRITE_MARGIN``),
so items repeat across polls: de-duplicate on ``kind`` and ``id``, and expect
an occasional item older than the newest one already shown.
